title: Matthew, looking back
tomorrow: where did the first churches meet, if not in churches?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the hard questions: Mary's grief at Jesus's feet, and Jesus weeping before he fixed a thing. Love enters.

Graduation cards love one line: we'll always be with you. Matthew's Gospel opens and closes on a version of it. In chapter one, Matthew quotes a prophet about the child's name: "Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." In the last verse, the risen Jesus stands on a mountain with his disciples and says: "lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world." So who is that last promise for? Christians have read it two ways.
screen: `WE'LL ALWAYS BE WITH YOU.` → `PAGE ONE: GOD WITH US.` → `LAST VERSE: WITH YOU ALWAY.`

segments.voice: View one: it's comfort, for anyone who needs it. The whole book is held between God with us and with you alway, and in the middle Jesus says, "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them." Not a stadium. Two or three at a kitchen table. On this reading the promise belongs to the lonely night and the hospital hallway, with no conditions attached. View two: it's a promise for the road. Read the sentence just before it: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations." Some readers call this the Great Commission. The presence comes with a job, said to people about to leave, and it's kept on the way: in the going, the teaching, the serving. Each side has a fair case. The first can point to the frame of the whole book, Emmanuel on page one. The second can point to the word therefore, and to the mountain where it's spoken to people about to scatter. And both keep this, from Matthew's story of the sheep and the goats. The King says, "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me." Comfort or commission, Matthew puts the presence in ordinary places, even a hungry stranger's face.
screen: `VIEW ONE: COMFORT, FOR ANYONE.` · `VIEW TWO: A PROMISE FOR THE ROAD.` · `BOTH: THE LEAST OF THESE.` · then, large: `WITH YOU ALWAYS.`

segments.voice: Walk ahead in your mind through the rest of today: the commute, the meal, the hard conversation, the quiet at the end. At each stop, pause and set the line down there, with you always, then move to the next.
Matthew. A Gospel held between two promises: God with us in its first chapter, and I am with you alway in its last verse.
Pocket this one: with you always, Matthew's last word on the matter, said on a mountain. Until tomorrow.
